title: The Blues
objective: After this level you can explain the blues form and where it came from.
summary: African Americans created the blues in the Deep South after the Civil War. Its 12-bar form uses three chords and AAB verses; blue notes fall between major and minor.

cards.headline: A bandleader waiting for a train heard a sound he'd build a career on.
cards.body: Around 1903, at the train station in Tutwiler, Mississippi, W.C. Handy heard a man singing while pressing a knife against his guitar strings. It was the blues. Handy, later known as the "Father of the Blues," went on to publish "The Memphis Blues" in 1912 and "St. Louis Blues" in 1914. So what exactly had he heard?

cards.headline: Born in the Deep South, out of the songs of slavery
cards.body: African Americans created the blues in the Deep South after the Civil War, and it was a recognizable genre by the 1890s. Its makers were formerly enslaved people and their children, many still working Southern plantations. Its raw material was Level 61's music: the three-line blues grew out of work songs, field calls, spirituals and folk ballads. The blues is what those songs became in the mouths of free people.

cards.headline: Say it, say it again, then answer it
cards.body: Most blues follow a 12-bar form built on just three chords: the tonic, the subdominant and the dominant. The words come in three-line stanzas. The second line more or less repeats the first, and the third finishes the thought with a new line that rhymes. It's call-and-response folded into one verse: you state your trouble, state it again, then deliver the punchline.

cards.headline: Blue notes live in the cracks between the keys
cards.body: Remember Level 7? A major third sits four semitones above the root, a minor third three, and a semitone is the smallest step on a keyboard. A blue note lowers the third, the seventh or sometimes the fifth by less than a semitone, so a blue third lands between major and minor, where a piano has no key. That's why the Tutwiler man's knife made sense: guitarists bend strings or slide a bar along them to reach the cracks.

mascot.line: A blue note isn't a wrong note. It lives between the keys, where a piano can't go.

cards.headline: The blues: explained
learned: Created by African Americans in the Deep South after the Civil War
Grew out of work songs, field calls and spirituals
Blue notes: bent pitches between major and minor

questions.prompt: In a classic blues stanza, what does the second line usually do?

options.label: Changes the key
options.rationale: The lines are about words, and line two repeats line one.

options.label: Asks a question the singer never answers
options.rationale: The third line finishes the thought.

options.label: Switches to a new subject
options.rationale: It more or less repeats the first line.

questions.explanation: Blues verses run AAB: a line, its repeat, then a new rhyming line that finishes the thought.

questions.prompt: Why can't a piano play a true blue third?

options.label: It's too high for the keyboard
options.rationale: It sits right between two neighboring keys, not off the end.

options.label: It lies between two neighboring keys
It needs two notes at once
options.rationale: A blue note is a single bent pitch.

options.label: It only exists on drums
options.rationale: Singers and guitarists make blue notes all the time.

questions.explanation: A blue note lowers the third by less than a semitone, the smallest keyboard step, so it lands between major and minor.

questions.prompt: From Level 58: what do the blues and Bahia's samba de roda share in their origins?

options.label: Both were first written down by European church composers
options.rationale: Neither began on paper; both grew from communities of enslaved Africans.

options.label: Both arrived with European immigrants
options.rationale: Samba de roda drew on enslaved Africans' traditions, the blues on formerly enslaved people's songs.

options.label: Both grew from enslaved Africans and their descendants
Both were invented in early recording studios
options.rationale: Both are older than recording and grew from communities of enslaved Africans.

questions.explanation: The blues was made by formerly enslaved people and their children, and samba de roda drew heavily on the traditions of Bahia's enslaved Africans.
